chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: Confronting Benny Goodman about where the drums sit
summary: Lee refused to sit far from the quintet at the Shrine, knocked on Goodman's dressing-room door, and got the drums placed where he wanted.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: So the next night at the Shrine, they set the stage up, and Red said, "Lee, Benny wants you to sit over there." Now we don't have but 5 men, and way over to the right,and I said, "Sit over where?" You know. "Over there." And I said, "What's .." -- I was sitting in the bend of the piano before, you know.

He said, "No, he don't want you to sit there. He wants you to sit over there." I said, "I'm not gonna sit over there." "Well ..." "I'm not gonna -- we don't have but 5 pieces, I'm not gonna sit way over there away from the other four." He said, "Well, that's where he wants you to sit."

Now Benny used to get to the concert about an hour ahead of time, and he was always warming up in the dressing room, you know, warming up in the dressing room, so it pays to be ignorant sometimes, you know -- I don't know what kind of cat he is, you know, but Mel Powell and Red Norva have been working with before, and I said, "Well, where is he?" They said, "Well, he's in the dressing room warming up." And I said,

"Well, I'm going to see him." He said, "Oh, no -- you're not supposed to bother him when he's warming up." I said, again, "If he wants some drums tonight, he's gonna be disturbed" and you know, he said, "Well, I wouldn't do it!"

So I knocked on the door and I said, "Benny," and he said, "Whay do you want?" You know. I said, "About the drums," -- "What about the drums?" I said, "I'm not gonna sit over there and play the drums." You know, "I want to be where I sat last night." He said, "Why do you want to be there?" I said, "Because we're closer together and I can hear everything, and I'm just not gonna play if I have to sit over there."

And he said, "Okay, go ahead and put the drums where you want them." So you know ... I didn't have the fear of him that they had, because they had been playing with him for years, and I had heard the stories about him, but I thought he was a nice cat, and I never had any problems with him -- that was the only thing that I ever had ...
He held no grudge or anything, huh?
No, oh no. When you hit the stage, it was all pleasurable, and I finished all the dates that he had asked me to play with him.
Why do you think he wanted the drums so far away?
I had no idea! Had no idea. Whatever it was, I never wanted to find out.
Did it have anything to do with the enormity of the Shrine stage for a 5 piece band?
No, the Shrine stage wasn't as large as the Long Beach stage, you know.

It wasn't that, but you know, he was -- well, that's the type person I never pursue anything if it's been cleared up, I don't ever -- I never would say, 'What was wrong with you that night?' As far as I was concerned, nothing was wrong with him because I got the drums where I wanted them, you know.
So that's really the way I feel about those types of things. And after that, what happened was ...
